note: Stefan Dušan's Serbian Empire (1346–1355) disintegrated rapidly after his death, fragmenting into regional lords — the most important being the Mrnjavčević brothers (controlling Macedonia), the Dejanović family, and eventually the Lazarević family's Serbian Despotate centered on Belgrade. Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović reassembled much of Serbia into a functioning state, only to die at Kosovo (1389). His son Stefan Lazarević became a Serbian Despot (1402) under Byzantine suzerainty — also serving as an Ottoman vassal. The Despotate's capital Smederevo fell in 1459, ending Serbian statehood for 360 years.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Serbian Empire's rapid fragmentation after Dušan's death demonstrates how personal empire without institutional consolidation collapses upon the founder's death; the transition from empire to despotate models the 'managed decline' of a medieval state under external pressure; the Kosovo myth (1389) creates the Serbian national narrative that outlasts the state by centuries
